The latest developments have raised concerns about the stability of the region and the potential for a wider conflict. The ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for international oil shipments, has further complicated these efforts.

The 2015 nuclear deal, also known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, was seen as a major breakthrough, but its future has been uncertain since the United States withdrew from the agreement. The situation in the Strait of Hormuz has significant implications for the global economy, as well as for regional stability. The waterway is a critical chokepoint for international oil shipments, and any disruption to traffic could have major consequences for the global economy. The United States has been seeking to build a coalition of nations to provide security for oil tankers in the region, but this effort has been met with skepticism by some countries.
